question: The calibration curves used in chemical analysis:

options.opa: They represent the response of an analytical method to unknown concentrations of analyte.
options.opb: They use standard samples that contain the solvent used in the analytical method, but without analyte.
options.opc: They use a standard solution that allows knowing the response of the analytical method to the interfering species that exist in the reagents.
options.opd: They are constructed by preparing samples of known analyte concentration (standards) and determining the response of the analytical procedure to these standards.
options.ope: They are constructed using samples of unknown analyte concentration and measuring the response of the analytical procedure to them.
